content.content:
What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
  `records` environment's deploy key.
- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

## Rulesets

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

## SSH signing for milestone tags (one-time setup, owner)

1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):
   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
2. Tell git to sign with it:
   ```sh
   git config --global gpg.format ssh
   git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub
   git config --global tag.gpgSign true
   ```
   Leave `commit.gpgSign` off: merges are signed by GitHub's button.
3. Let git verify signatures locally: add a line
   `<your git email> <contents of id_ed25519_signing.pub>` to
   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
   tag as **Verified**.

- Every file we write starts with an SPDX header:

  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
  repository is public and history is never rewritten.

## Privacy

The repository is public. No committed file, commit message or pull request
text names the owner's username, real name, e-mail address, hostname or
local folder names, or a full local path: write paths relative to the
repository, or as `~/...` with the top folder shown as `<top>`. Anyone who
finds such a term in the repository tells the owner instead of repeating it.

- **The terms** are kept by the owner, never in the repository: in the
  gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` (one per line, `#` comments,
  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which
  CI passes to the check.
- **The check** `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE, R-PUB-3) scans every
  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg
  hooks scan staged files and the message (`tools/install-hooks.sh` turns
  them on). A hit is reported by file and line only, never the term. CI
  fails when the secret is missing.
- **Records are scanned too** (since M1). Before a test record, an audit
  report or a C-MERGE re-check is hashed, uploaded or pushed, any file in
  it holding a term is withheld: deleted, and listed with the SHA-256 of
  the original in `WITHHELD.json`, which the record keeps (C-RECORD-PRIVATE).
  The original is not kept anywhere; the checks are deterministic, so it
  can be regenerated and matched to its hash. CI artifacts are kept 14 days.
- **Older records stay as they are.** A file under `sessions/` or
  `docs/prompts/` whose blob is identical to the same path at the base
  commit in `config/private-base` (the last main commit before the check)
  is exempt. This is decided from git's object hashes alone, so no session
  opens or lists the spec side's transcripts for it, and the check prints
  only how many files it exempted per folder. Every file added or changed
  after the base is checked in full. Files that sessions keep editing get no
  exemption: their current text is redacted instead (`docs/EXPOSURE.md` was,
  on 2026-10-22), and git history keeps the originals.
- **Archived transcripts** are redacted by `tools/archive-session.py`: the
  username anywhere it appears, the local top-level folder as `<top>`, and
  every private term.

## Low profile (for now)

The repository is public but unpromoted. In its name, description and topics,
and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),
  spec transcripts are skipped, not read, and the output says so;
- every transcript must show the SessionStart banner from
  `tools/session-banner.sh` with `status: OK`. Any `CONFIG MISMATCH` fails.
  The exemptions are listed by session ID in the check's `EXEMPT_NO_BANNER`,
  each with its reason (docs/EXPOSURE.md): the first session (M0a), M0a's
  one-prompt hook test, and the first spec session (M0b), each of which
  began before its folder had the banner hook;
- for clean-side transcripts, every file read, write, search, web fetch, web
  search and shell command is listed in the check's log by entry (the
  transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and any that touches
  forbidden material fails, named by rule ID (`F-...`, the check's
  `FORBIDDEN` table). The log never quotes a transcript: it goes into every
  test record, and the oldest archived transcripts still hold text that the

- Asked: 2026-10-23, session M4b (firmware side). Not a hardware question:
  the owner asked for it to be filed here, as a request about the audit's
  tooling, which the spec side keeps.
- Question: Add `vendor/plaits/` (Mutable Instruments' Plaits and stmlib,
  MIT, vendored unmodified at pinned upstream commits; pull request #59) to
  the similarity audit's base code, beside `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`
  (`audit/audit.json`, `base_code`; docs/AUDIT.md, "What is compared"), so
  that matches between a target and code we both took from Plaits are
  dropped. Our own glue in `firmware/demos/plaits/` stays compared.
- Why: M4b ports Plaits as a separate demo build (`firmware/demos/plaits/`)
  to measure the chip. `vendor/` is never compared as ours, but FM-1
  firmwares that ported Plaits would match our glue's calls into it, and
  any of its code a target copied would count against files of ours that
  include its headers. `base_code` takes one path today, so this needs a
  change to the audit tool or its settings, which are spec side. Read:
  docs/AUDIT.md, `audit/audit.json`.
- Status: open

### SR-5: Hardware single-precision floating point on the chip and in fwtest
- Asked: 2026-10-23, session M4b (firmware side)
- Question: (a) Does the AC791N's core execute the toolchain's hardware
  single-precision float instructions (its `fprev1` feature, enabled by
  clang's `-mfprev1`), and which of the toolchain's CPU models
  (`-mcpu=r1` to `r5`) is the chip's core? (b) Does fwtest model those
  instructions as the chip runs them (results, and the floating-point
  exception bits of HW-50's `EMU_MSG`), and at what cost: fwtest counts
  each as one cycle; how many cycles does each take on the chip (add,
  multiply, divide, square root, conversions, loads and stores)?
- Why: M4b measures Plaits (floats throughout) on our base. With our own
  soft-float a block of most engines costs 0.7 to 1.8 million of core 0's
  instructions, more than a block's 348 160 cycles: only one engine plays
  live. Built with `fprev1`, the same engines cost 10 000 to 52 000, and
  fwtest runs them with the same sound bit for bit (the bench's
  checksums). The SDK's own AC791N builds use `-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`
  (`apps/demo/demo_hello/board/wl82/Makefile` lines 74 and 75, at the
  pinned SDK commit; PROVENANCE P-29), which suggests the chip has them,
  but HARDWARE-SPEC.md says nothing about it, and M5's engine design
  (fixed or floating point, how many operators) depends on it. Read:
  HARDWARE-SPEC.md (HW-50's float exception bits), the toolchain's
  feature list, the SDK's Makefiles.
- Status: open

### SR-6: Running both cores on the chip
- Asked: 2026-10-23, session M4b (firmware side)
- Question: (a) When both cores run code from the code window and work in
  main RAM, what does each cost the other on the chip: shared caches or
  buses, wait states, and whether core 1 runs at the same clock as core 0
  (HW-11 gives fwtest's)? (b) What core 1 needs before it runs on the
  chip from a raw image (Q-11: the release, its cache and its MMU or
  protection set-up), and whether core 1 can take interrupts (its own
  `ICFG` and `ILAT` registers, HW-20 to HW-23, which fwtest has for core 0
  only). (c) Whether a plain store by one core is seen by the other's next
  load, or needs a barrier or a cache operation first.
- Why: M4b's bench starts core 1 (HW-9, HW-10) on a loop that renders a
  second Plaits voice when core 0 sets a word in RAM, and polls another for
  the result. In fwtest two voices at once take 0.50 to 0.55 of the time of
  one after the other on core 0, so core 1 nearly doubles what the
  firmware can play. M5 decides how to split voices between the cores, and
  needs to know how much of that holds on the chip. Read: HARDWARE-SPEC.md
  HW-8 to HW-11, HW-18 to HW-23, Q-11; docs/HARNESS.md ("Time": core 1's
  timer reads).
- Status: open

# Spec requests

How the firmware side (clean) asks the spec side (exposed) for a hardware
fact it needs, and how the answer comes back, without anything else passing
between them (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles").

## Asking (firmware side)

Add a request at the end of "Requests" below, by pull request:

- a number (`SR-1`, `SR-2`, ...; never reused);
- the date asked;
- the question: one fact about the hardware (an address, a bit, a pin, a
  timing, a protocol step, a limit), asked as narrowly as you can;
- why it is needed: what the firmware is trying to do, the milestone, and
  what you already tried or read (HARDWARE-SPEC.md sections, the JieLi SDK,
  FM-1-RE's documents, datasheets, your own black-box runs in fwtest);
- the status `open`.

Don't ask how another firmware does something, and don't paste or describe
any material you aren't allowed to read. A question about fwtest's
behaviour (a capture, an exit code, an option) is not a spec request: open
an issue or a pull request against docs/HARNESS.md.

## Answering (spec side)

- Answer by adding the fact to `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, with its source, as
  every fact there has (M0c's rules: facts only, never code or code
  structure; a fact whose only source is the emulator is marked so).
- Then set the request's status to `answered`, with a link to the section,
  in the same pull request. Nothing else goes in the request: no code, no
  explanation of how any other firmware or the emulator does it, no
  excerpts.
- If the fact isn't known, say so (`unknown`), with what would settle it
  (a probe on real hardware, a datasheet). If answering would take
  something the spec side may not pass on, say `declined` and why, in
  general terms.
- The spec side's text discipline applies to the whole exchange
  (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Spec-side text discipline"; C-SEP-TERMS checks it).

## Template

```markdown
### SR-<n>: <the question, in a few words>
- Asked: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <who or which session>
- Question: <one fact, asked narrowly>
- Why: <what the firmware needs it for; what was tried or read>
- Status: open | answered (HARDWARE-SPEC.md, "<section>") | answered in part (..., open: Q-n) | unknown | declined
- Answered: <YYYY-MM-DD>, <who or which session>
```

## Requests
### SR-3: The panel's wiring and SPI1's set-up on the chip; source 16 in fwtest
- Asked: 2026-10-22, session M2 (firmware side)
- Question: (a) On the chip, how SPI1 must be set up to drive the panel:
  its `CON` bits (mode, direction, enable) and `BAUD` (the clock it gives,
  and the fastest the panel takes), which pins carry its clock and data and
  the panel's chip select, and the `JL_IOMAP` selection and port set-up
  (direction, drive) for them and for PC8 (HW-30). (b) Whether the panel
  has a reset pin and a backlight pin, which, and their levels. (c) The
  panel's place in the controller's 240 x 320 memory (any row or column
  offset) for each `MADCTL` orientation, which orientation shows the
  picture upright as the FM-1 is held, and whether the panel needs display
  inversion (`0x21`) to show colours right. This is Q-6. (d) The longest
  transfer one write of `JL_SPI1->CNT` may ask for on the chip (the
  counter's width or limit). (e) In fwtest: a DMA transfer started with
  `CON` bit 13 clear still raises source 16 at its end, whatever the last
  write to `CON` held (our runs); HW-29 says bit 13 makes a finished
  transfer raise it. Which is right for the chip, and what fwtest does
  for single bytes written to `BUF`.
- Why: M2 brings up the panel and sends whole frames by DMA. In fwtest no
  set-up is needed (HW-29, HW-30), so M2 writes no SPI1 `CON` set-up bits,
  no `BAUD`, no pins, no reset or backlight, and leaves inversion off; it
  sends whole frames as 16-row chunks (7 680 bytes) because only 480-byte
  transfers are confirmed (E-5). Real hardware needs all of (a) to (d).
  For (e), the firmware's handler acknowledges a transfer it didn't chain,
  which is right under either behaviour, but the spec and fwtest disagree.
  Read: HARDWARE-SPEC.md sections 5 and 3, Q-6, the ST7789V datasheet
  (P-11, P-22), and `WL82.h`'s `JL_SPI_TypeDef` and port registers.
- Status: answered in part (HARDWARE-SPEC.md, "12. The LCD on the chip,
  and SPI1 in fwtest (SR-3)"): (a) in HW-55 and HW-56 (SPI1's pin groups,
  the group select, the port set-up registers, `CON`'s named bits, FM-1's
  own `CON` and `BAUD` values) and HW-57 (the panel's clock limit); (b)
  open, the panel's reset timing in HW-57; (c) open; (d) in HW-58; (e) in
  HW-59: the spec is right and fwtest was wrong. fwtest kept every `CON`
  bit once written, so after any write with bit 13 set, every transfer
  raised source 16 whatever `CON` was written to later. Fixed in fwtest
  0.2.0, which `config/fwtest-image` pins from the pull request that
  follows this answer: a `CON` write sets and clears bits as written,
  single bytes in `BUF` follow the same rule as DMA transfers, and a write
  of bit 14 alone also clears bit 13, so acknowledge by setting bit 14
  and keeping the other bits. Open: Q-6, Q-15.
- Answered: 2026-10-23, session SR-3 (spec side)

diff --git a/tests/test_separation.py b/tests/test_separation.py

+++ b/tests/test_separation.py
@@ -53,6 +53,94 @@ class EmulatorTermsTest(unittest.TestCase):
         self.assertNotIn("sha256", found, "words the clean side already used are not terms")
 
 
+class PlaitsTermsTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Since M4b (the owner's decision): the terms of vendor/plaits/, read
+    only from its checksum-verified files, are public, like the SDK's; the
+    check says how many emulator terms that takes off, and doesn't scan
+    vendor/plaits/ itself. Requirements: R-SEP-1"""
+
+    def write(self, path, text):
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(self.dir, path)), exist_ok=True)
+        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, path), "w") as f:
+            f.write(text)
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
+        # made-up words, built at run time
+        self.plaits_word, self.other = "plaits" + "_only_term", "nowhere" + "_else_term"
+        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.dir, "init", "-q", "-b", "main"], check=True)
+        self.write("vendor/emulator/model.rs", "%s %s\n" % (self.plaits_word, self.other))
+        self.write("vendor/plaits/eurorack/plaits/dsp/x.cc", "float %s;\n" % self.plaits_word)
+        self.sums()
+        self.write("docs/NOTES.md", "%s\n%s\n" % (self.plaits_word, self.other))
+        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.dir, "add", "-A"], check=True)
+        self.saved = (terms.ROOT, terms.EMU, terms.SDK, terms.REVIEWED, terms.baseline_texts, terms.PLAITS)
+        terms.ROOT, terms.EMU = self.dir, os.path.join(self.dir, "vendor", "emulator")
+        terms.SDK = terms.REVIEWED = os.path.join(self.dir, "none")
+        terms.PLAITS = os.path.join(self.dir, "vendor", "plaits")
+        terms.baseline_texts = lambda: iter(())
+        self.env = dict(os.environ)
+
+    def sums(self):
+        import hashlib
+        top = os.path.join(self.dir, "vendor", "plaits")
+        lines = []
+        for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(top):
+            for n in names:
+                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, n), top)
+                if rel != "SHA256SUMS":
+                    with open(os.path.join(dirpath, n), "rb") as f:
+                        lines.append("%s %s\n" % (hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest(), rel))

content.content:
Nobody working on this repository reads the targets. The spec side found
them from repository metadata alone. The job fetches them only inside CI,
and its logs and outputs hold scores and file names, never code. When the
job flags a pair, only an **auditor** may look (below).

## What is compared

- **Ours:** the C files under `firmware/` (`.c`, `.h`, and C++ suffixes if
  we ever have any). Assembly (`.S`) and linker scripts (`.ld`) are not
  compared: JPlag's C front end doesn't read them. `vendor/` is not ours
  and is never compared. A file of ours that JPlag cannot score at all is
  compared as text instead (below, "Files JPlag cannot score").
- **Base code:** the vendored JieLi SDK headers
  (`vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`). JPlag drops matches with base code, so
  code that both sides took from the SDK doesn't count against us.
- **Targets:** the C and C++ files of every target (below), at its pinned
  commit. `audit/targets.json` lists the targets; `paths` limits a target
  to some of its folders.
- **The control:** the C files of `raspberrypi/pico-examples` at tag
  `sdk-2.2.0`, commit `4c3a3dc0196dd426fddd709616d0da984e027bab`
  (BSD-3-Clause; `audit/audit.json`).

## The targets, from metadata only

`tools/audit-discover.py` builds `audit/targets.json` from
`audit/discover.json`. It asks GitHub's REST API, and `git ls-remote`, for
repository names, owners, descriptions, licences, languages, fork lists and
commit and tree SHAs. It never opens a target's files, README or web pages,
and never prints a description. A target is:

- **a seed:** Felucca (`hugelton/Felucca`), dinghy (`zvenson/dinghy`), the
  `fm1-sid/` and `probes/` folders of fm1-emu
  (`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`), M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, and the other
  FM-1 repositories of Felucca's author (`felucca-bsp`,
  `Felucca-Engines`, `Felucca-WebApp`, `felucca-mirror`);
- **a search hit:** a repository that one of the search queries finds and
  whose description names the FM-1, Felucca, GHOULBOX or Hortator. A
  repository that only matches by name must also be written in C or C++.
  "M-VAVE" or "dinghy" alone don't count, because they also name other
  products, boats and tools. dinghy's own lineage is found through its
  fork tree, and through descriptions that name the FM-1;
- **any fork of a target, to any depth.** A fork inherits its parent's
  `paths` and licence override.

**As found on 2026-10-22:** 780 repositories, after two passes whose
search results differed a little. Of these, 516 are scored and 262 are
duplicates by tree. The other 2 are empty. Of the 516 scored, 381 are classed `gpl`, 47
`permissive`, 43 `other` and 45 `none`.

The owner chose this wide net on 2026-10-22: every FM-1 repository, not
only Felucca's and dinghy's lineage. A target that turns out to be
unrelated costs only CI minutes. A target that is missed weakens the
claim.

Each target is **pinned** at its default branch's head commit, together
with that commit's tree. The job checks both. Targets whose tree (and
`paths`) is already in the list are marked `duplicate` and not fetched
again. Seeds come first, then other repositories, then forks, so a fork
that changed nothing is covered by the repository it copies. Empty
repositories are listed as `empty`.

Each target's **licence** is classed from its metadata as `gpl` (GPL,
LGPL, AGPL), `permissive` (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, WTFPL, CC0 and
similar), `other` (MPL-2.0, NOASSERTION, anything else) or `none` (no
licence). fm1-emu's metadata says MIT, but `fm1-sid/` is a GPL firmware
(docs/EXPOSURE.md), so that seed is classed `gpl`. The report shows each

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The similarity audit (R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-5; docs/AUDIT.md).

  audit.py run [--set full|fast] [--out DIR] [--jar FILE]
      Fetches each target in audit/targets.json at its pinned commit (C and
      C++ files only) into a temporary folder, with the control, and runs
      JPlag (pinned by hash, in a Java image pinned by digest, with no
      network) on our firmware and the control against them, the JieLi SDK
      as base code. Writes DIR/report.json and DIR/report.md: scores and
      file names only. Deletes everything it fetched, whatever happens.
      Exit status 1 if a check failed (the report says which).
  audit.py selftest [--out DIR] [--jar FILE]
      The same run against one made-up local target that holds verbatim
      copies of our files, and reformatted copies: each must be found, by
      JPlag or, for a file JPlag cannot score, by the text check
      (C-AUDIT-SELFTEST).
  audit.py check-artifact DIR
      Checks that DIR holds only a report this tool wrote (for the job that
      writes it into the record, which never sees the targets).

Nothing it prints or writes holds a line of a target's files: JPlag's own
output goes to a log in the temporary folder that is never shown, its
report archive (which embeds the sources) is read for names and numbers
only and then deleted, and before writing, every line of every target file
of at least `leak_line_chars` characters is looked for in the report
(C-AUDIT-LEAK).

A file of ours that JPlag cannot score (too few tokens, or not parsed) is
reported as such and compared as text instead: exact copies, and the share
of its normalised text found in each target file (C-AUDIT-TEXT).
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SCHEMA = 1
REQS = {
    "C-AUDIT-JPLAG": ["R-AUDIT-4"],
    "C-AUDIT-PIN": ["R-AUDIT-2"],
    "C-AUDIT-CONTROL": ["R-AUDIT-4"],
    "C-AUDIT-SCORE": ["R-AUDIT-1", "R-AUDIT-5"],
    "C-AUDIT-LEAK": ["R-AUDIT-1", "R-AUDIT-3"],
    "C-AUDIT-TEXT": ["R-AUDIT-1", "R-AUDIT-5"],
    "C-AUDIT-SELFTEST": ["R-AUDIT-5"],
}
GIT_ENV = dict(os.environ, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0", GIT_ADVICE="0")
SUB = re.compile(r"^(?:new_|pool_)?([ocp]\d{5}\.[A-Za-z]+)$")
# a string or character literal (kept), or a comment (dropped), for normalise()
LITERAL_OR_COMMENT = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])*\'|/\*.*?\*/|//[^\n]*', re.S)


        for v in obj:
            yield from report_strings(v)


def leak(texts, folder, min_chars):
    """The name of a file in folder one of whose lines (stripped, at least
    min_chars long) occurs in texts, or None."""
    joined = "\n".join(texts)
    windows = set(joined[i:i + min_chars] for i in range(max(0, len(joined) - min_chars + 1)))
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
        with open(os.path.join(folder, name), "rb") as f:
            text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        for line in text.splitlines():
            s = line.strip()
            if len(s) >= min_chars and s[:min_chars] in windows and s in joined:
                return name
    return None


def normalise(text):
    """C text without comments or whitespace, for the text check: string and
    character literals are kept, so a comment marker inside one stays."""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", LITERAL_OR_COMMENT.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if m.group(0)[0] in "\"'" else " ", text))


def grams(text, k):
    """The distinct k-character pieces of text (the whole text if shorter)."""
    return {text[i:i + k] for i in range(len(text) - k + 1)} or ({text} if text else set())


def text_scores(ours, folder, k):
    """The text check: for each of our files (name -> bytes), every file in
    folder (one per target blob) it is near: (ours, target, containment,
    exact), where containment is the share of our normalised text's
    k-character pieces found in the target file's, and exact means the same
    bytes. Pairs sharing nothing are left out."""
    mine = {}
    for n, data in ours.items():
        text = normalise(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        mine[n] = (data, text, grams(text, k))
    out = []
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
        with open(os.path.join(folder, name), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        text = normalise(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        theirs = None
        for n, (ob, ot, og) in mine.items():
            if not og:
                continue
            if ot in text:
                c = 1.0
            else:
                if theirs is None:
                    theirs = grams(text, k)
                c = len(og & theirs) / len(og)
            if c > 0 or data == ob:
                out.append((n, name, c, data == ob))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: (-x[3], -x[2], x[0], x[1]))


def not_scorable(state, cfg):
    """Why JPlag could not score a file of ours, for the report."""
    why = {"TOO_SMALL": "fewer tokens than JPlag's minimum match of %d" % cfg["min_tokens"],
           "CANNOT_PARSE": "JPlag's C front end could not parse it"}.get(state, "JPlag reports it as %s" % state)
    return "not scorable by JPlag: %s (%s); compared by the text check instead" % (why, state)


def text_row(x, ours_names, where, licences, limit=10):
    """A text-check pair for the report: our file, the scores and the target
    files (repository and path) holding that blob."""
    o, p, c, exact = x
    places = [{"repo": r, "path": path, "licence_class": licences.get(r, "none")} for r, path in where.get(p, [])]
    return {"ours": ours_names.get(o, o), "containment": round(c, 4), "exact": exact,
            "target_files": places[:limit] if limit else places, "target_places": len(places)}


def pair_row(x, ours_names, where, licences, limit=10):
    """A pair for the report: our file's path, the scores, and the target files
    (repository and path) holding that blob, the first `limit` of them."""
    o, p, l, m, v = x
    places = [{"repo": r, "path": path, "licence_class": licences.get(r, "none")} for r, path in where.get(p, [])]
    return {"ours": ours_names.get(o, o), "longest_tokens": l, "max": round(m, 4), "avg": round(v, 4),
            "target_files": places[:limit] if limit else places, "target_places": len(places)}


def run(cfg, targets_doc, set_name, out, jar=None, selftest=None):
    """One audit. selftest: a list of target dicts used instead of targets_doc's."""
    t0 = time.time()
    checks = {}
    base_tmp = os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-", dir=base_tmp)
    report = {"schema": SCHEMA, "set": set_name, "commit": os.environ.get("GITHUB_SHA") or
              git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], ROOT).stdout.decode().strip(),
              "run": ("%s/%s/actions/runs/%s" % (os.environ["GITHUB_SERVER_URL"], os.environ["GITHUB_REPOSITORY"],
                                                os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ID"]) if os.environ.get("GITHUB_RUN_ID") else None),
              "jplag": {"version": cfg["jplag"]["version"], "sha256": cfg["jplag"]["sha256"]},
              "java_image": cfg["java_image"], "margin_tokens": cfg["margin_tokens"],
              "control_ceiling_tokens": cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], "min_tokens": cfg["min_tokens"]}
    try:
        for d in ("new", "base"):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(work, d))
        jar_path, got = get_jar(cfg, work, jar)
        jar_ok = got == cfg["jplag"]["sha256"] and "@sha256:" in cfg["java_image"]
        checks["C-AUDIT-JPLAG"] = ("PASS" if jar_ok else "FAIL",
                                   "jar sha256 %s; Java image pinned by digest" % ("matches" if jar_ok else "differs: " + got))
        if not jar_ok:
            raise RuntimeError("JPlag is not the pinned jar")
        ours = copy_tree_files(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"]), cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "o")
        for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"])):
            for f in files:
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"]))
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(work, "base", rel)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(work, "base", rel))
        c = cfg["control"]
        ctl_dir = os.path.join(work, "control")
        problems = []
        try:
            fetch(c["url"], c["commit"], c["tree"], ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"])
        except (Unavailable, Mismatch) as e:
            problems.append("control %s: %s" % (c["repo"], e))
        control = copy_tree_files(ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "c")
        shutil.rmtree(ctl_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        report["control"] = {"repo": c["repo"], "commit": c["commit"], "licence": c["licence"], "files": len(control)}

        all_targets = selftest if selftest is not None else targets_doc["targets"]
        chosen = [t for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == "scored" and (set_name != "fast" or t["repo"] in cfg["fast"])]
        pool = Pool(os.path.join(work, "pool"))
        licences = {t["repo"]: t.get("licence_class", "none") for t in all_targets}
        rows = []

        def fetch_one(i, t):
            tdir = os.path.join(work, "t%05d" % i)
            try:
                url = t["url"] if selftest is not None else t["url"] + ".git"
                return tdir, fetch(url, t["commit"], t.get("tree"), tdir, cfg["suffixes"], t.get("paths")), None
            except (Unavailable, Mismatch) as e:
                return tdir, None, e

        # fetched side by side, but added to the pool in the list's order, so its names are stable
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=cfg.get("fetch_workers", 8)) as ex:
            futures = [ex.submit(fetch_one, i, t) for i, t in enumerate(chosen)]
            for t, fut in zip(chosen, futures):
                tdir, files, err = fut.result()
                row = {"repo": t["repo"], "commit": t["commit"], "licence": t.get("licence"),
                       "licence_class": t.get("licence_class", "none")}
                if err is None:
                    new = 0
                    for blob, path in files:
                        _, is_new = pool.add(blob, os.path.join(tdir, path), t["repo"], path)
                        new += is_new
                    row.update({"fetched": True, "files": len(files), "new_files": new})
                elif isinstance(err, Mismatch):
                    row.update({"fetched": False, "why": "tree mismatch: " + str(err)})
                    problems.append("%s: tree mismatch" % t["repo"])
                else:
                    row.update({"fetched": False, "why": str(err)})
                shutil.rmtree(tdir, ignore_errors=True)
                rows.append(row)
        unavailable = [r["repo"] for r in rows if not r["fetched"] and not r.get("why", "").startswith("tree")]
        checks["C-AUDIT-PIN"] = ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS",
                                 "%d targets fetched at their pinned commit and tree; %d unavailable%s"
                                 % (sum(r["fetched"] for r in rows), len(unavailable),
                                    ("; " + "; ".join(problems)) if problems else ""))
        report["targets"] = rows
        if targets_doc and selftest is None:
            report["unresolved"] = [u["name"] for u in targets_doc.get("unresolved", [])]
            report["not_scored"] = {s: sum(1 for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == s)
                                    for s in ("duplicate", "empty", "unreachable")}
        report["pool_files"] = len(pool.where)

        if not pool.where:
            raise RuntimeError("no target files were fetched")
        code = run_jplag(cfg, work)
        result = os.path.join(work, "result.jplag")
        if code or not os.path.exists(result):
            raise RuntimeError("JPlag failed (exit %d); its log is not shown, as it can quote the files" % code)
        pairs, failed, tokens = read_results(result)
        os.remove(result)
        s = score(pairs, cfg, pool.where)
        names = dict(ours)
        names.update(control)
        # JPlag leaves a file that matched nothing (no run of min_tokens) out
        # of its index, so its token count is unknown; it was still compared.
        report["ours_files"] = [{"file": p, "tokens": tokens.get(n), "state": failed.get(n, "scored" if n in tokens else "no match")}
                                for n, p in sorted(ours.items())]
        # A file JPlag could not score at all goes to the text check instead;
        # a file it scored that matched nothing ("no match") does not.
        unscorable = sorted(n for n in ours if n in failed)
        for f, n in zip(report["ours_files"], sorted(ours)):
            if n in failed:
                f["not_scorable"] = not_scorable(failed[n], cfg)
        tc = cfg["text_check"]
        mine = {}
        for n in unscorable:
            with open(os.path.join(work, "new", n), "rb") as fh:
                mine[n] = fh.read()
        text = text_scores(mine, pool.dir, tc["k"]) if mine else []
        text_flagged = [x for x in text if x[3] or x[2] >= tc["threshold"]]
        best_text = {}
        for x in text:
            best_text.setdefault(x[0], x)
        report["text_check"] = {"k": tc["k"], "threshold": tc["threshold"], "files": [ours[n] for n in unscorable],
                                "best": [text_row(best_text[n], ours, pool.where, licences) if n in best_text else
                                         {"ours": ours[n], "containment": 0.0, "exact": False, "target_files": [],
                                          "target_places": 0} for n in unscorable],
                                "top_pairs": [text_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in text[:cfg["top_pairs"]]],
                                "flagged": [text_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences, limit=None) for x in text_flagged]}
        text_check = ("FAIL" if text_flagged else "PASS",
                                  ("%d of our files not scorable by JPlag (%s), compared as text with %d target files; "
                                   "%d pairs an exact copy or at or above %.2f of %d-character pieces"
                                   % (len(unscorable), ", ".join(ours[n] for n in unscorable), len(pool.where),
                                      len(text_flagged), tc["threshold"], tc["k"])) if unscorable else
                                  "every file of ours was scored by JPlag; none needed the text check")
        report["control_max_tokens"] = s["control_max"]
        report["threshold_tokens"] = s["threshold"]
        report["top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in s["ours"][:cfg["top_pairs"]]]
        report["control_top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, control, pool.where, licences) for x in s["control"][:5]]
        report["ours_vs_control_best"] = ([{"ours": ours.get(x[0]), "control": control.get(x[1]), "longest_tokens": x[2],
                                            "max": round(x[3], 4)} for x in s["ours_control"][:3]])
        by_repo_ours, by_repo_ctl = {}, s["control_per_target"]
        for x in s["ours"]:
            for r, _ in pool.where.get(x[1], []):
                by_repo_ours[r] = max(by_repo_ours.get(r, 0), x[2])
        unparsed = {}
        for n, state in failed.items():
            for r, _ in pool.where.get(n, []):
                unparsed.setdefault(r, {}).setdefault(state.lower(), 0)
                unparsed[r][state.lower()] += 1
        for row in rows:
            row["ours_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ours.get(row["repo"], 0)
            row["control_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ctl.get(row["repo"], 0)
            row["not_parsed"] = unparsed.get(row["repo"], {})
        accepted_rules = load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "accepted.json")).get("accepted", []) \
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "accepted.json")) else []
        flagged, accepted = split_accepted([pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences, limit=None) for x in s["flagged"]],
                                           accepted_rules)
        s["flagged"] = flagged
        report["flagged"] = flagged
        report["accepted"] = accepted
        report["control_related"] = s["related"]
        fetched = sum(r["fetched"] for r in rows)
        ctl_ok = bool(control) and len(s["related"]) <= cfg["control_related_share"] * max(fetched, 1)
        checks["C-AUDIT-CONTROL"] = ("PASS" if ctl_ok else "FAIL",
                                     "%d control files; its longest match with an unrelated target %d tokens; "
                                     "%d of %d targets control-related (above %d tokens; at most %d%% allowed)"
                                     % (len(control), s["control_max"], len(s["related"]), fetched,
                                        cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], round(100 * cfg["control_related_share"])))
        checks["C-AUDIT-SCORE"] = ("FAIL" if s["flagged"] else "PASS",
                                   "%d of our file pairs above %d tokens (the control's %d plus %d; for a "
                                   "control-related target, its own score plus %d)%s"
                                   % (len(s["flagged"]), s["threshold"], s["control_max"], cfg["margin_tokens"],
                                      cfg["margin_tokens"],
                                      "; %d more accepted by an auditor's finding" % len(accepted) if accepted else ""))
        checks["C-AUDIT-TEXT"] = text_check
        if selftest is not None:
            report["selftest"] = {"ours_best": [[ours.get(x[0], x[0])] + list(x[1:]) for x in s["ours"]],
                                  "text": [[ours.get(x[0], x[0]), pool.where[x[1]][0][1], x[2], x[3]] for x in text]}
        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        write_report(report, checks, out, pool.dir, cfg)
    except Exception as e:  # the report says what failed; nothing from the targets is printed
        checks.setdefault("C-AUDIT-SCORE", ("FAIL", "not scored: %s" % e))
        report["error"] = str(e)
        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        pool_dir = os.path.join(work, "pool")
        write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir if os.path.isdir(pool_dir) else None, cfg)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    gone = not os.path.exists(work)
    print("temporary folder removed: %s" % ("yes" if gone else "NO"))
    return report, checks


def traceability(checks):
    table = []
    for req in sorted(set(r for rs in REQS.values() for r in rs)):
        mine = [c for c, rs in REQS.items() if req in rs and c in checks]
        res = [checks[c][0] for c in mine]
        table.append({"requirement": req, "checks": mine,
                      "result": "FAIL" if "FAIL" in res else "PASS" if res else "not run"})
    return table

def write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir, cfg):
    report["checks"] = [{"id": k, "result": v[0], "detail": v[1], "reqs": REQS[k]} for k, v in checks.items()]
    report["traceability"] = traceability(checks)
    md = markdown(report)
    text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    if pool_dir:
        hit = leak([md] + list(report_strings(report)), pool_dir, cfg["leak_line_chars"])
        report["checks"].append({"id": "C-AUDIT-LEAK", "result": "FAIL" if hit else "PASS", "reqs": REQS["C-AUDIT-LEAK"],
                                 "detail": "a line of a target file is in the report; report withheld" if hit else
                                 "no line of a target file (%d characters or more) in the report" % cfg["leak_line_chars"]})
        if hit:
            report = {k: report[k] for k in ("schema", "set", "commit", "run", "checks")}
        report["traceability"] = traceability({c["id"]: (c["result"], "") for c in report["checks"]})
        md = markdown(report)
        text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(text + "\n")
    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(md)


def markdown(r):
    L = ["# Similarity audit %s" % (r.get("commit") or "")[:12], "",
         "- Set: %s; run: %s" % (r.get("set"), r.get("run") or "local"),
         "- JPlag %s (sha256 `%s`), Java image `%s`" % (r.get("jplag", {}).get("version"),
                                                        r.get("jplag", {}).get("sha256", "")[:16], r.get("java_image", "")),
         ""]
    if "threshold_tokens" in r:
        L += ["- Control: %s at `%s`, %s files" % (r["control"]["repo"], r["control"]["commit"][:12], r["control"]["files"]),
              "- The control's longest match with any target it is not related to: **%d tokens**; a pair of ours "
              "fails above **%d tokens** (margin %d)." % (r["control_max_tokens"], r["threshold_tokens"], r["margin_tokens"]),
              "- Control-related targets (the control matches them above %d tokens; each judged against the "
              "control's own score there plus the margin): %s" % (r["control_ceiling_tokens"],
                                                                  ", ".join(r.get("control_related", [])) or "none"),
              "- Target files scored: %d (one copy per blob)" % r.get("pool_files", 0), ""]
    if r.get("error"):
        L += ["**Not scored:** %s" % r["error"], ""]
    L += ["## Checks", "", "| Check | Result | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for c in r.get("checks", []):
        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
    if r.get("flagged"):
        L += ["", "## Flagged pairs (an auditor compares these; nobody else opens them)", "",
              "| Our file | Target | Path | Licence | Longest | Max |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in r["flagged"]:
            for t in p["target_files"]:
                L.append("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], t["path"], t["licence_class"],
                                                               p["longest_tokens"], p["max"]))
    if "top_pairs" in r and not r["top_pairs"]:
        L += ["", "## Our top file pairs", "", "None: no file of ours shares a run of %d tokens or more with any target file."
              % r.get("min_tokens", 12)]
    if r.get("top_pairs"):
        L += ["", "## Our top file pairs", "", "| Our file | Target (places with this file) | Path | Licence | Longest | Max | Avg |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in r["top_pairs"]:
            t = p["target_files"][0] if p["target_files"] else {"repo": "?", "path": "?", "licence_class": "?"}
            L.append("| %s | %s (%d) | %s | %s | %d | %.3f | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], p["target_places"], t["path"],
                                                                     t["licence_class"], p["longest_tokens"], p["max"], p["avg"]))
    if r.get("ours_files"):
        L += ["", "## Our files", "", "| File | Tokens | State |", "|---|---|---|"]
        for f in r["ours_files"]:
            L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (f["file"], f["tokens"] if f["tokens"] is not None else "-",
                                           f.get("not_scorable", f["state"])))
    tc = r.get("text_check")
    if tc and tc["files"]:
        L += ["", "## The text check (our files JPlag cannot score)", "",
              "Each is compared with every target file, one per blob: the share of its normalised text's "
              "%d-character pieces found in the target file (containment), and whether the bytes are the same "
              "(exact). A pair fails at %.2f or above, or when exact." % (tc["k"], tc["threshold"]), "",
              "| Our file | Target (places with this file) | Path | Licence | Containment | Exact |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in tc["top_pairs"] or tc["best"]:
            t = p["target_files"][0] if p["target_files"] else {"repo": "-", "path": "-", "licence_class": "-"}
            L.append("| %s | %s (%d) | %s | %s | %.3f | %s |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], p["target_places"], t["path"],
                                                               t["licence_class"], p["containment"],
                                                               "yes" if p["exact"] else "no"))
        if tc["flagged"]:
            L += ["", "Flagged by the text check (an auditor compares these; nobody else opens them):", "",
                  "| Our file | Target | Path | Licence | Containment | Exact |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
            for p in tc["flagged"]:
                for t in p["target_files"]:
                    L.append("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %.3f | %s |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], t["path"], t["licence_class"],
                                                                  p["containment"], "yes" if p["exact"] else "no"))
    if r.get("targets"):
        L += ["", "## Targets", "", "| Target | Commit | Licence | Files (new) | Ours longest | Control longest | Not parsed |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for t in r["targets"]:
            if t.get("fetched"):
                np = ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(t.get("not_parsed", {}).items())) or "0"
                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | %d (%d) | %s | %s | %s |" % (
                    t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t["files"], t["new_files"],
                    t.get("ours_longest_tokens", "-"), t.get("control_longest_tokens", "-"), np))
            else:
                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | not fetched: %s | | | |" % (t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t.get("why")))
    if "not_scored" in r:
        L += ["", "Not scored: %s. Unresolved (no repository found): %s." % (
            ", ".join("%d %s" % (v, k) for k, v in r["not_scored"].items()), ", ".join(r.get("unresolved", [])) or "none")]
    L += ["", "## Traceability", "", "| Requirement | Checks | Result |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for t in r.get("traceability", []):
        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (t["requirement"], ", ".join(t["checks"]), t["result"]))
    L.append("")
    return "\n".join(L)


def reformat(text):
    """A near-exact copy for the self-test: no comments, each line
    re-indented, and a comment of its own at the top, so the bytes differ."""
    text = LITERAL_OR_COMMENT.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if m.group(0)[0] in "\"'" else " ", text)
    lines = ["\t" + line.strip() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#") else line.strip()
             for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return "/* reformatted */\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def selftest_target(work_parent, cfg):
    """A made-up local target: verbatim and reformatted copies of our files
    and one unrelated file, in a git repository served by path. Returns
    (target dict, its folder)."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-selftest-", dir=work_parent)
    src = os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"])
    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(src):
        for f in files:
            if wanted(f, cfg["suffixes"]):
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), src)
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "copied", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(d, "copied", rel))
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "reformatted", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
                with open(os.path.join(dirpath, f), encoding="utf-8") as fin, \
                        open(os.path.join(d, "reformatted", rel), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fout:
                    fout.write(reformat(fin.read()))
    with open(os.path.join(d, "unrelated.c"), "w") as f:
        f.write("int unrelated(int a) { return a * 3 + 1; }\n")
    env = dict(GIT_ENV, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]",
               GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]")
    for args in (["init", "-q"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "selftest"],
                 ["config", "uploadpack.allowFilter", "true"], ["config", "uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant", "true"]):
        subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=d, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
    commit = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    tree = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    return {"repo": "selftest/copy-of-ours", "url": "file://" + d, "commit": commit, "tree": tree,
            "status": "scored", "licence_class": "none"}, d


def selftest_verdict(report, cfg):
    """Every one of our files must be found in the made-up target, and the
    report written. A file JPlag scored: by a match covering at least 90% of
    its tokens. A file JPlag cannot score: by the text check, as an exact copy
    (the verbatim one) and at or above its threshold without being exact (the
    reformatted one). A file JPlag scored but matched nowhere fails."""
    files = report.get("ours_files", [])
    tokens = {f["file"]: f["tokens"] for f in files if f["state"] == "scored"}
    best = {}
    for o, p, l, m, v in report.get("selftest", {}).get("ours_best", []):
        best[o] = max(best.get(o, 0), l)
    by_jplag = [f for f, t in tokens.items() if best.get(f, 0) >= 0.9 * t]
    exact, near = set(), set()
    for o, path, c, is_exact in report.get("selftest", {}).get("text", []):
        if is_exact:
            exact.add(o)
        elif c >= cfg["text_check"]["threshold"]:
            near.add(o)
    by_text = [f["file"] for f in files if "not_scorable" in f and f["file"] in exact & near]
    leak_ok = any(c["id"] == "C-AUDIT-LEAK" and c["result"] == "PASS" for c in report.get("checks", []))
    found = len(by_jplag) + len(by_text)
    ok = bool(files) and found == len(files) and leak_ok
    return ok, "%d of our %d files found in a target holding copies of them (%d by JPlag, %d by the text check); " \
        "leak check %s" % (found, len(files), len(by_jplag), len(by_text), "PASS" if leak_ok else "not passed")


def check_artifact(folder):
    names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
    if names != ["report.json", "report.md"]:
        return ["unexpected files: %s" % names]
    problems = []
    for n in names:
        if os.path.getsize(os.path.join(folder, n)) > 2 << 20:
            problems.append("%s is too large" % n)
    r = load_json(os.path.join(folder, "report.json"))
    if r.get("schema") != SCHEMA or not isinstance(r.get("checks"), list):
        problems.append("report.json is not an audit report")
    return problems


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["run", "selftest", "check-artifact"])
    ap.add_argument("dir", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--set", default="full", choices=["full", "fast"])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "audit"))
    ap.add_argument("--jar")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "audit.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--targets", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "targets.json"))
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.command == "check-artifact":
        problems = check_artifact(a.dir)
        for p in problems:
            print("FAIL %s" % p)
        print("artifact: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
        return 1 if problems else 0
    cfg = load_json(a.config)
    if a.command == "selftest":
        t, d = selftest_target(os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None, cfg)
        try:
            report, checks = run(cfg, None, "selftest", a.out, a.jar, selftest=[t])
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
        ok, detail = selftest_verdict(report, cfg)
        print("C-AUDIT-SELFTEST: %s (%s)" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", detail))
        for c in report.get("checks", []):
            print("  %s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
        return 0 if ok else 1
    report, checks = run(cfg, load_json(a.targets), a.set, a.out, a.jar)
    for c in report.get("checks", []):
        print("%s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
    failed = [c["id"] for c in report.get("checks", []) if c["result"] != "PASS"]
    print("audit: %s" % ("FAIL (%s)" % ", ".join(failed) if failed else "PASS"))
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

  MIT notice in its own header (checked file by file at these commits:
  127 source files, all "Copyright 2012" to "2021 Emilie Gillet", MIT);
  `stmlib/LICENSE` states it for stmlib. stmlib's third-party code (ST's

class Pool:
    """Target files, one copy per blob: pool/p00001.c ..., and where each came from."""

    def __init__(self, folder):
        self.dir = folder
        os.makedirs(folder)
        self.by_blob = {}
        self.where = {}

    def add(self, blob, src, repo, path):
        new = blob not in self.by_blob
        if new:
            name = "p%05d%s" % (len(self.by_blob) + 1, os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower())
            shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(self.dir, name))
            self.by_blob[blob] = name
            self.where[name] = []
        name = self.by_blob[blob]
        self.where[name].append((repo, path))
        return name, new


def copy_tree_files(top, suffixes, dest, prefix):
    """Our files (or the control's): dest/<prefix>00001.c ..., and a map to their paths."""
    names = {}
    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(top):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d != ".git")
        for f in sorted(files):
            full = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, top).replace(os.sep, "/")
            if wanted(rel, suffixes) and os.path.isfile(full):
                name = "%s%05d%s" % (prefix, len(names) + 1, os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower())
                shutil.copyfile(full, os.path.join(dest, name))
                names[name] = rel
    return names

    """Our files JPlag cannot score are compared as text: exact copies, and
    the share of their normalised text in each target file.
    Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-AUDIT-5"""

    OURS = (b"/* our glyphs, a made-up font */\n#include \"sb.h\"\n"
            b"#define G(a, b) { ROW(a), ROW(b) }\n"
            b"const u8 glyphs[4][2] = {\n"
            b"    /* 'a' */ G(\".#.#.\", \"#...#\"),\n"
            b"    /* 'b' */ G(\"##...\", \"..#..\"),\n"
            b"    /* 'c' */ G(\"...##\", \".###.\"),\n"

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)

        return {p: (round(c, 3), exact) for o, p, c, exact in audit.text_scores({"o00001.c": self.OURS}, self.dir, 24)}

        text = self.OURS.decode()
        self.put("p00001.c", self.OURS)
        self.put("p00002.c", audit.reformat(text).encode())
        self.put("p00003.c", b"static int before(int x) { return x + 1; }\n" + self.OURS +
                 b"int after(void) { return before(2); }\n")
        self.put("p00004.c", b"int unrelated(int a) { return a * 3 + 1; }\n")
        half = "\n".join(l for l in text.splitlines() if "'c'" not in l and "'d'" not in l)
        self.put("p00005.c", half.encode())
        got = self.scores()
        self.assertEqual(got["p00001.c"], (1.0, True), "a verbatim copy is exact")
        self.assertEqual(got["p00002.c"], (1.0, False), "a reformatted copy is found, but not as exact")
        self.assertEqual(got["p00003.c"], (1.0, False), "a copy inside a larger file is found")
        self.assertNotIn("p00004.c", got, "unrelated code shares nothing")
        self.assertTrue(0 < got["p00005.c"][0] < 1, got["p00005.c"])

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

"""Our own analysis of fwtest's audio captures (M4; tools/fw-suite.py,
R-AUD-*). Python's standard library only: `wave` reads the file, the rest
is written here (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M4, "How the sound is measured").

- The rate: fwtest's WAV header says 44 100 Hz, but the output plays a
  frame every 544 ticks of 24 MHz (HW-45), 44 117.647 Hz; every
  frequency here is computed at that rate (RATE).
- sine_fit: a four-parameter least-squares fit of a sine (amplitude,
  phase, offset and frequency), refined by Gauss-Newton steps from a
  first guess counted from zero crossings. Its frequency is the
  measurement; its residual is THD+N's distortion and noise.
- clicks: the largest second difference of the samples, against what a
  sine of that amplitude and frequency can give under the instrument's
  linear ramps. A step (a hard start or stop) gives a second difference
  of about the step itself, many times the bound.
"""
import math
import struct
SUB = re.compile(r"^(?:new_|pool_)?([ocp]\d{5}\.[A-Za-z]+)$")
# a string or character literal (kept), or a comment (dropped), for normalise()
LITERAL_OR_COMMENT = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])*\'|/\*.*?\*/|//[^\n]*', re.S)


def load_json(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


def sha256_file(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()


def wanted(path, suffixes, paths=None):
    if not path.lower().endswith(tuple(suffixes)):
        return False
    return not paths or any(path.startswith(p) for p in paths)


def git(args, cwd):
    """Runs git quietly: its output is never shown (it could name a target's contents)."""
    return subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=GIT_ENV)

`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio
### Files JPlag cannot score: the text check

JPlag drops a submission it cannot score: one with fewer tokens than its
minimum match (`TOO_SMALL`), or one it cannot parse (`CANNOT_PARSE`). A
file of ours dropped like that is never compared by the gate above. Since
M2 one is: `src/font.c`, our font, is a single constant table whose rows
are macro calls on string literals, and JPlag's C front end makes 5 tokens
of its 116 lines. Such a file is not left out:

- the report lists it under "Our files" as **not scorable by JPlag**, with
  JPlag's reason;
- the **text check** (C-AUDIT-TEXT) compares it with every target file, one
  copy per blob, and reports two scores per pair:
  - **exact:** the same bytes;
  - **containment:** the share of our file's distinct 24-character pieces
    that occur in the target file, both sides normalised first: comments
    removed (the SPDX header included), then all whitespace. String and
    character literals are kept. Containment, not a symmetric ratio,
    because a copy may sit inside a larger target file.
- The check **fails** on an exact copy, or at a containment of **0.5** or
  more. Like the gate, it fails whatever the target's licence, and only
  an auditor looks at a flagged pair.

Only files JPlag dropped go to the text check. A file JPlag scored that
matched nothing (`no match`) was compared by the gate; it is not sent
here. Which files go is decided by each run's JPlag output, so a new file
that JPlag cannot score is covered without a change here. Its rows hold
names and numbers only, and the leak check reads them like the rest of the
report.

**Why 24 characters and 0.5.** Before choosing, the spec side ran the
check on the same calibration pair as the gate: every pico-examples file
### The report

`report.json` and `report.md` hold:
- the pinned JPlag, Java image and control, the control's highest longest
  match with an unrelated target, the threshold and the margin, and the
  control-related targets;
- the checks (C-AUDIT-JPLAG, -PIN, -CONTROL, -SCORE, -TEXT, -LEAK) and
  their traceability to R-AUDIT-*;
- **our top 20 file pairs**: our file, the target repositories and paths
  holding the matched file (the first ten of them, and how many there are),
  each with its licence class, and the longest match, max and avg;
- the control's top five pairs, and its best pair with our own files;
- each of our files' token counts. A file that matched nothing anywhere
## Files

| File | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `audit/discover.json` | Seeds, search queries, the mention rule, unresolved names. |
| `audit/targets.json` | Every target, pinned: commit, tree, licence class, status. Written by `tools/audit-discover.py`. |
| `audit/audit.json` | JPlag and the Java image (pinned), the control (pinned), base code, the margin, the ceiling, the text check's piece length and threshold, the fast set. |

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none. Session SR-1-SR-2 (spec side, 2026-10-22) added sections 9 to 11 for
SR-1 and SR-2, which are answered in part; what stays open is Q-2, Q-13
and Q-14. Session SR-3 (spec side, 2026-10-23) added section 12 for SR-3,
answered in part (open: Q-6, Q-15), and section 13, which confirms HW-41's
fwtest part for M3.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources

| Key | Source |
|-----|--------|
| SDK | JieLi AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), commit `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, Apache-2.0 (PROVENANCE P-2, P-10). `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` are vendored in `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/`; the other files cited are at the same commit and path prefix. Line numbers refer to that commit. |
| RE | AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL), commit `ec832f281ca165a7d5e0722985f3acb1465046d5`: its hardware and boot documents `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md`, `docs/io/01-boot.md`, `docs/io/03-audio-dac.md`, `docs/io/08-display.md`, `docs/io/09-storage.md` (PROVENANCE P-9). Only their hardware facts are used here. |
| DS | Sitronix ST7789V datasheet, version 1.3 (2014-03), 316 pages, from `https://www.newhavendisplay.com/appnotes/datasheets/LCDs/ST7789V.pdf`, SHA-256 `8ecf0e43…5d04ca1` (PROVENANCE P-11). Page numbers as printed. |
| PANEL | The FM-1's printed panel labels, from two sources that agree: the owner's screenshot of the F-Emulator app's panel with its default labels, `docs/sources/panel-app-default-labels.png` (secondary: the app's drawing of the panel); and M-VAVE's product photo of the FM-1, `https://www.m-vave.com/images/products/fm-1.webp` on `https://www.m-vave.com/product.html?id=fm-1`, accessed 2026-10-22, SHA-256 `e610a746…df14b95`, not copied into this repository (PROVENANCE P-12). Only the printed labels are taken from them. The owner chose these two sources. |
| HARNESS | docs/HARNESS.md, fwtest's manual. It is the spec side's own description of fwtest, so it never confirms an entry on its own. |
| E-n | A spec-side black-box experiment: a small image run in fwtest (the pinned image, `config/fwtest-image`). Its result is stated in the entry. C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS re-runs every one in CI, so a cited result that stops holding fails CI. |

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none. Session SR-1-SR-2 (spec side, 2026-10-22) added sections 9 to 11 for
SR-1 and SR-2, which are answered in part; what stays open is Q-2, Q-13
and Q-14. Session SR-3 (spec side, 2026-10-23) added section 12 for SR-3,
answered in part (open: Q-6, Q-15), and section 13, which confirms HW-41's
fwtest part for M3.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources

| Key | Source |
|-----|--------|
| SDK | JieLi AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), commit `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, Apache-2.0 (PROVENANCE P-2, P-10). `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` are vendored in `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/`; the other files cited are at the same commit and path prefix. Line numbers refer to that commit. |
| RE | AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL), commit `ec832f281ca165a7d5e0722985f3acb1465046d5`: its hardware and boot documents `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md`, `docs/io/01-boot.md`, `docs/io/03-audio-dac.md`, `docs/io/08-display.md`, `docs/io/09-storage.md` (PROVENANCE P-9). Only their hardware facts are used here. |
| DS | Sitronix ST7789V datasheet, version 1.3 (2014-03), 316 pages, from `https://www.newhavendisplay.com/appnotes/datasheets/LCDs/ST7789V.pdf`, SHA-256 `8ecf0e43…5d04ca1` (PROVENANCE P-11). Page numbers as printed. |
| PANEL | The FM-1's printed panel labels, from two sources that agree: the owner's screenshot of the F-Emulator app's panel with its default labels, `docs/sources/panel-app-default-labels.png` (secondary: the app's drawing of the panel); and M-VAVE's product photo of the FM-1, `https://www.m-vave.com/images/products/fm-1.webp` on `https://www.m-vave.com/product.html?id=fm-1`, accessed 2026-10-22, SHA-256 `e610a746…df14b95`, not copied into this repository (PROVENANCE P-12). Only the printed labels are taken from them. The owner chose these two sources. |
| HARNESS | docs/HARNESS.md, fwtest's manual. It is the spec side's own description of fwtest, so it never confirms an entry on its own. |
| E-n | A spec-side black-box experiment: a small image run in fwtest (the pinned image, `config/fwtest-image`). Its result is stated in the entry. C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS re-runs every one in CI, so a cited result that stops holding fails CI. |
